summary.verdict: The implementation conforms to the Decision Core / Inference Engine contract. It consumes activated inference cases and phase contracts, emits only inference records, tension records, gap agendas and validation agendas, preserves provenance, lineage and version metadata, handles synthetic-only and conflicting evidence conservatively, and does not verify claims or produce final reports.

findings: Inputs match the functional contract: inference_cases must be structured lists of activated motor_013 cases, and phase_contracts must authorize inference_cases plus all four motor_014 output classes.

Outputs match the contract: each accepted case produces one InferenceRecord, zero or more Tension records, one GapAgenda and one ValidationAgenda with phase contract references and rule version metadata.

The implementation rejects non-activated cases, missing or contradictory phase contracts, missing required output authorization, malformed list inputs, duplicate or empty case identifiers, and evidence references without provenance or lineage.

Synthetic-only support remains hypothesis_only and creates downstream validation needs instead of being promoted to evidence. Conflicting evidence creates an explicit conflict tension, unresolved-conflict gap and validation item rather than silently selecting a winner.
The output contract guard rejects forbidden report, verification, field evidence and decision-grade fields, keeping the motor inside its inferential handoff responsibility.

Top-level emitted records include motor_id, case_id, phase_contract_ref, contract_version, lineage_refs, rule_version, created_at, updated_at, version_id, version_hash, source_ref, produced_by_motor, produced_at and parent_id.
EvidenceRef objects preserve evidence_id, source_class, evidence_level, provenance_ref and lineage_ref; missing identity, provenance or lineage blocks emission with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED.
Stable identifiers and version hashes are derived from canonical content, contract version, rule version, lineage and parent context, with runtime timestamp fields excluded from hash comparison.
Lineage refs include case lineage plus activation record, trigger log and phase contract references, supporting downstream reconstruction without mutating upstream records.

test_results.coverage_assessment: The documented test specification covers happy path, sparse case, malformed input, edge cases, pass criteria and fail criteria. A no-bytecode executable smoke exercise ran seven assertions against the implementation: bounded inference happy path, missing-validation gap creation, deterministic version hash repeatability, sparse contextual evidence blocked_by_gap behavior, synthetic-only hypothesis_only behavior, conflict tension creation and provenance rejection.
test_results.notes: No standalone test runner was added or modified during conformance review. The smoke exercise imported the implementation with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 to avoid writing cache files and used the documented phase contract and case shapes from the artifacts.
